The second: it is the Fire, which covers the faces of the disbelievers. This was said by Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Qurazi, and Muqatil.

The first: they are the faces of the Jews and the Christians. This was said by Ibn Abbas.

The second: they are all the disbelievers. This was said by Yahya ibn Salam.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Laboring, weary﴾ On this there are four views.

The first: they are those who labored and toiled in the world without the religion of Islam, such as the idol-worshippers and the disbelievers among the People of the Book, like the monks and others. This was narrated by Ata' from Ibn Abbas.

The second: they are the monks and the people of the monasteries. This was narrated by Abu al-Duha from Ibn Abbas, and Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Zayd ibn Aslam said likewise.

The third: they are laboring and weary in the Fire, through handling chains and shackles, because they did not labor for God in the world, so He makes them labor and weary in the Fire. al-Awfi narrated this meaning from Ibn Abbas, and al-Hasan said likewise. Qatadah said: they were arrogant in the world toward obedience to God, so He makes them labor and weary in the Fire by moving from one punishment to another. al-Dahhak said: they are required to climb a mountain in the Fire. Ibn al-Sa'ib said: they fall upon their faces in the Fire. Muqatil said: they labor in the Fire, eating from the Fire, and are weary from punishment.

The fourth: they labor in the world with sins and are weary in the Fire on the Day of Resurrection. This was said by Ikrimah and al-Suddi. The discourse here concerns the faces, and what is meant is their owners. We have already explained the meaning of "nasab" (weariness) in His saying: ﴿No fatigue touches them therein﴾ [al-Hijr: 48].

(p-96) His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Roasting at a fierce fire﴾ The people of Basra and Asim, except Hafs, read "tusla" with a dammah on the ta'. The rest read it with a fathah. Ibn Abbas said: it has been heated, and it blazes against the enemies of God. ﴿Given to drink from a boiling spring﴾ That is, extremely hot. al-Hasan said: Hellfire has been kindled over it since it was created, so they are driven into it as thirsty herds.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They will have no food except from darie'﴾ On this there are six views.

The first: it is a thorny plant lying flat upon the ground, which the Quraysh call "al-Shibriq." When it dries, they call it "darie'." This was narrated by al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas, and Mujahid, Ikrimah, and Qatadah said likewise.

The second: it is a tree of fire. This was narrated by al-Walibi from Ibn Abbas.

The third: it is stones. This was said by Ibn Jubayr.

The fourth: it is al-Salam. This was said by Abu al-Jawza'.

The fifth: in this world it is dry thorn that has no leaves, and in the Hereafter it is thorn of fire. This was said by Ibn Zayd.

(p-97) The sixth: it is a food to which they humble themselves before God. This was said by Ibn Kaysan.

The commentators said: When this verse was revealed, the polytheists said: "Our camels grow fat on the darie'!" So God revealed: ﴿Which neither nourishes nor satisfies hunger﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: their couches are of gold, adorned with emeralds, pearls and rubies, raised high. When their occupants have not yet come, they remain raised, but when the one who owns it wishes to sit on it, it lowers itself for him until he sits on it, and then it rises back to its place. ﴿And cups set in place﴾ ready for them. We have already mentioned "al-akwāb" (cups) in [al-Zukhruf: 71]. ﴿And cushions arranged﴾, which are the pillows; their singular is "numruqah" with a damma on the nūn. His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿How it was created﴾. Ali ibn Abi Talib, Ibn 'Abbas, Abu al-'Aliyah, Abu 'Imran, and Ibn Abi 'Ablah read "khalaqtu" with a fatha on the khā' and a damma on the tā'.

They also read "rafa'tu", "naṣabtu" and "saṭaḥtu" in the same way.

[p-100] His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And at the sky, how it was raised﴾ from the earth, so that nothing can reach it, without pillars. ﴿And at the mountains, how they were set firm﴾ upon the earth, so that they do not move or change. ﴿And at the earth, how it was spread out﴾, meaning spread flat. "Al-saṭḥ" is the spreading of a thing, and all of this points to the power of its Creator. ﴿So remind﴾, meaning admonish. ﴿You are only a reminder﴾, meaning an admonisher. At that time there was no command other than reminding, and His saying, may He be exalted, indicates this: ﴿You are not over them a controller﴾, meaning a dominator who would kill them and compel them to believe. Then it was abrogated (naskh) by the verse of the sword (āyat al-sayf). Abu Razin, Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, 'Ikrimah, Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Halwani from Ibn 'Amir read "bi-musayṭir" with a sīn. The explanation of "al-muṣayṭir" has already been given in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Or are they the controllers?﴾ [al-Tur: 37].

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Except whoever turns away﴾. This is a disjunctive exception, meaning: "but whoever turns away" ﴿and disbelieves﴾ after being reminded. Ibn 'Abbas, 'Amr ibn al-'As, Anas ibn Malik, Abu Mijlaz, Qatadah, and Sa'id ibn Jubayr read "ala man tawalla" with a fatha on the hamzah and a light lām. ﴿Then Allah will punish him with the greatest punishment﴾, which is that He will cause him to enter Hell. This is because they were punished in the world with hunger, killing and captivity, so the punishment of Hell is the greatest. ﴿Indeed, to Us is their return﴾. Ubayy ibn Ka'b, 'Aishah, 'Abd al-Rahman, and Abu Ja'far read "iyyābahum" with a doubled yā', meaning their return and their destination after death. ﴿Then indeed, upon Us is their reckoning﴾. Muqatil said: meaning their recompense.
